# Bring PCL's GPU KinectFusion and people-detection modules to CUDA 12.8 (RTX 5090) `/workspace` contains three repositories (each its own git repo): | repo | what it is | |---|---| | `pcl` | The Point Cloud Library at upstream commit `c47198828`. Its GPU stack:
• `gpu/containers` and `gpu/utils`: device arrays, texture helpers, warp and block primitives
• `gpu/octree`, `gpu/features`, `gpu/surface`
• the applications `gpu/kinfu` (KinectFusion), `gpu/kinfu_large_scale` (KinectFusion with a moving cyclical volume) and `gpu/people` (random-forest body-part detection, including vendored NVIDIA NCV / NPP-staging primitives) | | `kinfu_replay` | A downstream tool that runs KinFu and KinFu large-scale on synthetic depth sequences with known ground truth. It reports poses, TSDF statistics, meshes, extracted clouds and timing, and can run several trackers concurrently (`--concurrent`). | | `people_eval` | A downstream tool that runs the people detector on an RGB-D frame and its variants (`people_eval`, with `--threads` for concurrent detectors), and exercises the NCV / NPP-staging primitives (`ncv_check`). | The lab's new machine has an **RTX 5090 (Blackwell, sm_120)**, which needs **CUDA 12.8** or later, and that is the only toolkit installed (`/usr/local/cuda`). On CUDA 12, PCL's CMake disables `gpu_kinfu`, `gpu_kinfu_large_scale` and `gpu_people` ("uses textures which was removed in CUDA 12"); see upstream issues #5571 and #5995. The code was written for pre-Volta GPUs. **Make these three modules, and everything they depend on, build and run correctly on CUDA 12.8 / sm_120.** The two tools must keep working unchanged. ## Requirements 1. **Builds on CUDA 12.8.** - `pcl` configures and builds with CUDA 12.8 for sm_120, with `gpu_kinfu`, `gpu_kinfu_large_scale` and `gpu_people` enabled by default. - No texture or surface *references* remain anywhere in the GPU modules. You may use texture objects or other memory paths. - All device code (SASS and PTX) must target sm_120: do not lower the architecture, rely on JIT of an older target, or vendor another CUDA toolkit. 2. **Same results as the original pre-CUDA-12 code.** The original was built with CUDA 11.8, run on this GPU through PTX JIT, and recorded: - People detector body-part labels must match **exactly**, run with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`. - The NCV / NPP-staging primitives exercised by `ncv_check` must produce **bit-identical** buffers. That covers integral images (also from unaligned sources), decimation, rectangle std-dev, separable filters, resize and frame interpolation, plus compaction and transpose. - KinFu and KinFu large-scale must track and reconstruct as well as the original, measured against ground truth. Their TSDF volumes, meshes and extracted clouds must agree with the original's to within floating-point noise. 3. **Correct on independent thread scheduling.** - The modernized kernels must not depend on implicit warp-synchronous execution. - `compute-sanitizer` must report nothing on the KinFu, KinFu large-scale, people and NCV workloads with `--tool racecheck`, `--tool synccheck` and `--tool memcheck`. 4. **Safe for concurrent use.** - Several `KinfuTracker`, `kinfuLS::KinfuTracker`, `MarchingCubes` and `PeopleDetector` instances may run at the same time from different host threads. - Every result must then be bitwise identical to running each alone. 5. **Much faster than the original.** The lab moved to this GPU to run these pipelines faster.     template<bool testFG> __device__ __forceinline__ Label 
    evaluateTree(int u, int v, float f, int treeHeight, int numNodes, const Node* nodes, const Label* leaves)
    {
      int    depth = tex2D(depthTex, u, v);

      float  scale = f / depth;

      // go down the tree
      int nid = 0;
      for(int nodeDepth = 0; nodeDepth < treeHeight; ++nodeDepth)
      {
        const Node node = nodes[nid];

        const AttribLocation& loc = node.loc;
        int d1 = tex2D (depthTex, u + loc.du1 * scale, v + loc.dv1 * scale);
        int d2 = tex2D (depthTex, u + loc.du2 * scale, v + loc.dv2 * scale);

        if (testFG)
        {
          if( d1 - depth > constFGThresh ) 
            d1 = std::numeric_limits<short>::max();

          if( d2 - depth > constFGThresh ) 
            d2 = std::numeric_limits<short>::max();
        }

        int delta = d1-d2;
        bool test = delta > (int)node.thresh;
        if( test ) nid = nid*2+2;
        else       nid = nid*2+1;
      }
      return leaves[nid-numNodes];
    }

int
pcl::device::computeOffsetsAndTotalVertexes (DeviceArray2D<int>& occupied_voxels)
{
  thrust::device_ptr<int> beg (occupied_voxels.ptr (1));
  thrust::device_ptr<int> end = beg + occupied_voxels.cols ();

  thrust::device_ptr<int> out (occupied_voxels.ptr (2));
  thrust::exclusive_scan (beg, end, out);

  int lastElement, lastScanElement;

  DeviceArray<int> last_elem (occupied_voxels.ptr(1) + occupied_voxels.cols () - 1, 1);
  DeviceArray<int> last_scan (occupied_voxels.ptr(2) + occupied_voxels.cols () - 1, 1);

  last_elem.download (&lastElement);
  last_scan.download (&lastScanElement);

  return lastElement + lastScanElement;
}

        int total = tasksH + tasksV;
